mlb-diamondbacks.text: Fun fact. The Diamondbacks were eliminated on the last day of the season — that's three straight Octobers without a playoff trip in the desert.
mlb-diamondbacks.claim: Arizona missed the playoffs for a third straight season in 2026, eliminated on the final day of the regular season.
mlb-diamondbacks.proof: On September 27 (the last day of the season), the Diamondbacks were eliminated from playoff contention, and extending their drought of a playoff spot to three seasons.

mlb-diamondbacks.text: Fun fact. Arizona's 2023 pennant run ended in five quick games — Texas had the World Series wrapped up by November 1.
mlb-diamondbacks.claim: The Diamondbacks lost the 2023 World Series to the Texas Rangers in five games, ending on November 1.
mlb-diamondbacks.proof: The series began on October 27 and ended on November 1 with Texas winning in five games.

mlb-diamondbacks.text: Fun fact. Arizona's 2023 pennant came just two seasons removed from a 110-loss year that included an MLB-record 24 straight road losses.
mlb-diamondbacks.claim: Two seasons before the 2023 pennant, the Diamondbacks lost 110 games, including an MLB-record 24 consecutive road losses.
mlb-diamondbacks.proof: The Diamondbacks were just two seasons removed from a 110–loss season, which included an MLB-record 24 straight road losses.

mlb-diamondbacks.text: Fun fact. In 2024 the Diamondbacks won 89 games and missed the playoffs anyway — nudged out on a tiebreaker by Atlanta and the Mets.
mlb-diamondbacks.claim: The 2024 Diamondbacks finished 89–73 but missed the playoffs because they lost the tiebreaker to the Braves and Mets.
mlb-diamondbacks.proof: ... season with a record of 89–73, an improvement on their 84–78 from 2023 ... However, they missed the playoffs due to losing the tiebreaker against the Atlanta Braves and New York Mets.

mlb-diamondbacks.text: Fun fact. Arizona's 2025 season was snuffed out by a loss to the Padres on September 26 — playoff hopes, gone.
mlb-diamondbacks.claim: The Diamondbacks were eliminated from playoff contention on September 26, 2025, with a loss to San Diego.
mlb-diamondbacks.proof: On September 26, with a loss to the San Diego Padres, the team was eliminated from playoff contention.

mlb-braves.text: Fun fact. The Braves led the 2020 NLCS 3–1, before the Dodgers became the fourteenth team in postseason history to come back from a 3–1 series deficit.
mlb-braves.claim: The Braves blew a 3–1 series lead in the 2020 NLCS, which the Dodgers won in seven games.
mlb-braves.proof: The Dodgers defeated the Braves in seven games, winning their third National League pennant in four seasons. The Dodgers were the fourteenth team in postseason history to come back from a 3–1 series deficit.

mlb-braves.text: Fun fact. The Yankees swept the 1999 Series in four games — their third straight Fall Classic win over the Braves franchise, who batted just .200.
mlb-braves.claim: The Braves were swept 4–0 in the 1999 World Series by the Yankees, the Yankees' third straight Fall Classic win over the Braves franchise, and Atlanta batted .200 in the series.
mlb-braves.proof: The Yankees swept the 1999 Series in four games for their second consecutive title, third in four years, and 25th overall ... It was the Yankees' third straight defeat of the Braves franchise in the Fall Classic ... The powerhouse Braves batted just .200 in the 4-game Series.

mlb-braves.text: Fun fact. One year after returning to the postseason, the Braves suffered a historic September collapse to miss the 2011 playoffs.
mlb-braves.claim: In 2011, the season after Bobby Cox's final 2010 season that saw the Braves return to the postseason, the Braves suffered a historic September collapse and missed the playoffs.
mlb-braves.proof: Bobby Cox's final year as manager in 2010 saw the Braves return to the postseason for the first time since 2005 ... The next season, the Braves suffered a historic September collapse to miss the postseason.

mlb-braves.text: Fun fact. After winning their first division title in 1969, the Braves were promptly swept by the 'Miracle Mets' in the National League Championship Series.
mlb-braves.claim: In 1969 the Braves won their first division title, then were swept by the 'Miracle Mets' in the National League Championship Series.
mlb-braves.proof: After arriving in Atlanta in 1966, the Braves found success in 1969, winning the first National League West Division title with the onset of divisional play. In the National League Championship Series the Braves were swept by the "Miracle Mets".

mlb-braves.text: Fun fact. The Braves' worst season ever came in 1935: a dismal 38–115 record.
mlb-braves.claim: The Braves finished the 1935 season with a dismal 38–115 record, the franchise's worst season.
mlb-braves.proof: The Braves finished the season with a dismal 38–115 record, marking the franchise's worst season.

mlb-orioles.text: Fun fact. The Orioles' last World Series appearance came in 1983 — followed by 14 consecutive losing seasons between 1998 and 2011. The 90s were rough.
mlb-orioles.claim: Orioles have not reached a World Series since 1983 and had 14 consecutive losing seasons 1998-2011
mlb-orioles.proof: Since their last World Series appearance in 1983, the Orioles have struggled to sustain success, including suffering 14 consecutive losing seasons between 1998 and 2011.

mlb-orioles.text: Fun fact. In 1988 the Orioles lost the first 21 games of the season — the low point of a decline that began right after their 1983 World Series win.
mlb-orioles.claim: Orioles lost their first 21 games in 1988, at the end of a decline following the 1983 World Series win
mlb-orioles.proof: After the 1983 World Series win, the Orioles experienced a decline, culminating in the 1988 season where they lost the first 21 games.

mlb-orioles.text: Fun fact. The 2018 Orioles lost 115 games — the most in franchise history. Somebody check if the scoreboard still works.
mlb-orioles.claim: 2018 Orioles lost 115 games, the most in franchise history
mlb-orioles.proof: the 2018 season saw the Orioles lose 115 games, the most in franchise history

mlb-orioles.text: Fun fact. The 2023 Orioles' "successful season" ended with the team losing three straight games to the Texas Rangers in the playoffs. Swept.
mlb-orioles.claim: 2023 ALDS: Orioles lost three straight to Texas, a series sweep
mlb-orioles.proof: the team's successful season ended in the postseason American League Division Series, with the Orioles losing three straight games to the Texas Rangers. The series sweep was the first time since the 2022 season that the Orioles had been swept in a series.

mlb-orioles.text: Fun fact. From 1901 through the end of 2026, the Orioles' all-time record is 9,274–10,253–110 (.475). Even the franchise's own history can't call them winners.
mlb-orioles.claim: Franchise all-time win-loss record 9,274-10,253-110 (.475) through end of 2026
mlb-orioles.proof: From 1901 through the end of 2026, the franchise's overall win–loss record is 9,274–10,253–110 (.475).

mlb-redsox.text: Fun fact. Red Sox fans once endured an 86-year wait between World Series championships. Literally a lifetime of heartbreak before 2004.
mlb-redsox.claim: Red Sox endured an 86-year wait for their next World Series title, won in 2004
mlb-redsox.proof: The Sox endured an 86-year wait before the team's sixth World Series championship in 2004.

mlb-redsox.text: Fun fact. In Game 6 of the 1986 World Series, the Shea Stadium scoreboard briefly congratulated the Red Sox as World Series champions. Famous last words.
mlb-redsox.claim: Shea Stadium scoreboard briefly congratulated Boston as champions during Game 6 of the 1986 World Series
mlb-redsox.proof: A message even appeared briefly on the Shea Stadium scoreboard congratulating the Red Sox as World Series champions. After so many years of abject frustration, Red Sox fans around the world could taste victory.

mlb-redsox.text: Fun fact. The 2011 Red Sox became the first team in MLB history to blow a 9-game lead in the division heading into September, going 7–20 in the final month.
mlb-redsox.claim: 2011 Red Sox blew a 9-game September lead, went 7-20, missed the playoffs
mlb-redsox.proof: In 2011, the Red Sox collapsed, becoming the first team in MLB history to blow a 9-game lead in the division heading into September, going 7–20 in the final month and failing again to make the playoffs.

mlb-redsox.text: Fun fact. Fresh off the 2013 title, the Red Sox finished last in the AL East in 2014 (71–91) and again in 2015 (78–84). Champions to cellar in one year.
mlb-redsox.claim: Red Sox finished last in AL East in 2014 with 71-91 and again in 2015 with 78-84, right after the 2013 championship
mlb-redsox.proof: Following the 2013 championship, the team finished last in the AL East during 2014 with a record of 71–91, and again in 2015 with a record of 78–84.

mlb-redsox.text: Fun fact. The Red Sox finished last in their division in both 2022 and 2023 — with the exact same 78–84 record. Consistency at rock bottom.
mlb-redsox.claim: Red Sox finished last in the division in 2022 and 2023, both seasons 78-84
mlb-redsox.proof: The 2022 season was much less successful, with the team finishing in last place within their division with a 78–84 record, the first losing record for the team in a 162-game season since 2015. In 2023, the Red Sox once again finished in last place in their division with a 78–84 record.

mlb-cubs.text: Fun fact. The Cubs once went 108 years without a World Series title — a record drought in MLB that wasn't snapped until 2016.
mlb-cubs.claim: The Cubs' 108-year World Series championship drought was a record drought in Major League Baseball and was ended in 2016.
mlb-cubs.proof: the Cubs won the 2016 National League Championship Series and 2016 World Series, which ended a 71-year National League pennant drought and a 108-year World Series championship drought,[6] both of which are record droughts in Major League Baseball.[7][8]

mlb-cubs.text: Fun fact. In the 2015 NLCS the Cubs were swept in four games by the Mets, keeping them from their first World Series since 1945.
mlb-cubs.claim: The Cubs were swept in four games by the Mets in the 2015 NLCS and were unable to reach their first World Series since 1945.
mlb-cubs.proof: However, they were swept in four games by the Mets and were unable to make it to their first World Series since 1945.[77]

mlb-cubs.text: Fun fact. The 2019 Cubs lost nine straight games in late September, missed the playoffs entirely — the first time they'd failed to qualify since 2014.
mlb-cubs.claim: A nine-game losing streak in late September 2019 contributed to the Cubs being eliminated from playoff contention — the first time they had failed to qualify since 2014.
mlb-cubs.proof: The team's postseason chances were compromised after suffering a nine-game losing streak in late September.[97] The Cubs were eliminated from playoff contention on September 25, marking the first time the team had failed to qualify for the playoffs since 2014.[98]

mlb-cubs.text: Fun fact. The 2026 Cubs went 89-73 and finished second in their division behind the Brewers — for the second year in a row.
mlb-cubs.claim: In the 2026 season the Cubs finished 89-73, second in their division behind the Brewers for the second consecutive year.
mlb-cubs.proof: The 2026 season saw the Cubs finish with a record of 89-73, placing second in their division behind the Brewers for the second year in a row.

mlb-cubs.text: Fun fact. The 2012 Cubs lost 101 games — their worst record since 1966.
mlb-cubs.claim: The 2012 Cubs lost 101 games, their worst record since 1966.
mlb-cubs.proof: Although the team had a dismal 2012 season, losing 101 games (the worst record since 1966), it was largely expected.

mlb-whitesox.text: Fun fact. The White Sox lost their 121st game in 2024 — the most losses in modern MLB history — and the record-breaker came against Detroit. You're welcome, Mets fans.
mlb-whitesox.claim: White Sox lost their 121st game of 2024 to Detroit, surpassing the 1962 Mets for most losses in modern MLB history.
mlb-whitesox.proof: On September 27, the White Sox lost their 121st game of the season to the Detroit Tigers, surpassing the 1962 New York Mets for the most losses in modern MLB history.

mlb-whitesox.text: Fun fact. Chicago dropped 21 straight games in 2024 — the first 21-game losing streak since the 1988 Orioles. That's a streak, not a slump.
mlb-whitesox.claim: White Sox lost 21 consecutive games in 2024; first team since the 1988 Orioles to endure a 21-game losing streak.
mlb-whitesox.proof: The streak continued, and on August 5, the White Sox lost their 21st consecutive game. This marked the first time since the 1988 Baltimore Orioles that a team endured a 21-game losing streak.

mlb-whitesox.text: Fun fact. On August 17, 2024, the White Sox became the first team eliminated from playoff contention — the earliest such clinch since the divisional era began in 1969. Efficiency!
mlb-whitesox.claim: White Sox were the first team eliminated from playoff contention in 2024 (August 17), the earliest such elimination since the divisional era began in 1969.
mlb-whitesox.proof: On August 17, with their loss to the Houston Astros, the White Sox became the first team to be eliminated from playoff contention in 2024. This surpassed the 2018 Baltimore Orioles for the earliest clinch of missing the playoffs since the divisional era began in 1969.

mlb-whitesox.text: Fun fact. In 2024 the Sox hit 100 losses on August 25 — the fastest any team has gotten there since the 1916 Athletics. Summer was just getting started.
mlb-whitesox.claim: White Sox lost their 100th game on August 25, 2024; fastest team to 100 losses since the 1916 Philadelphia Athletics.
mlb-whitesox.proof: on August 25, the White Sox became the fastest team since the 1916 Philadelphia Athletics to lose 100 games in a season when they lost to their division rival Detroit Tigers, dropping them to 31–100.

mlb-whitesox.text: Fun fact. The White Sox clinched their third consecutive losing season in August 2025. At least they're fast at clinching things.
mlb-whitesox.claim: White Sox clinched their third consecutive losing season in August 2025 (after a 1–0 loss on August 20).
mlb-whitesox.proof: Despite this, the team clinched their third consecutive losing season after a 1–0 loss on August 20 to the Atlanta Braves.

mlb-reds.text: Fun fact. No MLB team has gone longer without winning a playoff series than the Reds — their last series win came back in 1995.
mlb-reds.claim: The Reds currently have the longest drought of not winning a playoff series of any MLB team, with their last series win coming in 1995.
mlb-reds.proof: currently have the longest drought of not winning a playoff series of any MLB team, with their last win coming in 1995.

mlb-reds.text: Fun fact. The Reds haven't won a World Series in 36 years — their last title came all the way back in 1990.
mlb-reds.claim: The World Series championship droughts table lists the Reds at 36 years with their last title in 1990 (current through the 2026 season).

mlb-reds.text: Fun fact. In the 2012 NLDS the Reds took a 2–0 lead, then lost three straight at home — the first NL team since the 1984 Cubs to lose a division series after leading 2–0.
mlb-reds.claim: In the 2012 NLDS the Reds led 2-0, then lost three straight at their home ballpark, becoming the first NL team since the 1984 Cubs to lose a division series after leading 2-0.
mlb-reds.proof: However, they lost three straight at their home ballpark, becoming the first National League team since the Chicago Cubs in 1984 to lose a division series after leading 2–0.

mlb-reds.text: Fun fact. The Reds closed 2013 with six consecutive losses — including a wild-card playoff loss to the Pirates at PNC Park — and then fired Dusty Baker.
mlb-reds.claim: The Reds ended the 2013 season with six consecutive losses, including the NL wild-card loss to Pittsburgh at PNC Park, and then fired Dusty Baker.
mlb-reds.proof: Following six consecutive losses to close out the 2013 season, including a loss to the Pittsburgh Pirates at PNC Park in the National League wild-card playoff game, the Reds decided to fire Dusty Baker.

mlb-reds.text: Fun fact. The Reds haven't won the NL Central since 2012 — a 14-year division-title drought.
mlb-reds.claim: The division-champion droughts table lists the Reds at 14 years in the NL Central with their last division title in 2012 (current through the 2026 season).

mlb-guardians.text: Fun fact. Cleveland's last World Series title came in 1948 — still the longest active championship drought among MLB's 30 teams. Ask a museum.
mlb-guardians.claim: Guardians' World Series title drought dating to 1948 is the longest active among the 30 current MLB teams.
mlb-guardians.proof: The team's World Series championship drought, dating to 1948, is the longest active among the 30 current Major League teams.

mlb-guardians.text: Fun fact. The 2016 Indians led the World Series 3–1, then lost Game 7, 8–7, in ten innings to the Cubs. Peak Cleveland.
mlb-guardians.claim: Game 7 of the 2016 World Series was won by Chicago 8–7 in ten innings; the Cubs came back from a 3–1 series deficit (i.e., Cleveland led 3–1).
mlb-guardians.proof: The deciding seventh game, won by Chicago 8–7 in ten innings, was the fifth World Series Game 7 to go into extra innings, and the first since 1997 … The Cubs became the first team to come back from a 3–1 deficit to win the Series since the 1985 Kansas City Royals.

mlb-guardians.text: Fun fact. Cleveland lost the 1997 World Series on a Game 7 walk-off in extra innings — handing the Marlins their first-ever title. Salt, meet wound.
mlb-guardians.claim: Marlins beat the Indians 4–3 to win their first World Series; Game 7 was decided in extra innings on a walk-off single by Édgar Rentería.
mlb-guardians.proof: The Marlins, who were underdogs, defeated the Indians, four games to three, to win their first World Series championship. Game 7 was decided in extra innings on a walk-off single hit by Édgar Rentería.

mlb-guardians.text: Fun fact. Cleveland only won the 2025 AL Central when Detroit lost on the final day — then lost the Wild Card Series to those same Tigers, 2–1.
mlb-guardians.claim: Guardians won the AL Central when the Tigers lost on the final day; then the Tigers won the Wild Card Series 2–1 over Cleveland.
mlb-guardians.proof: In the AL Central, the Guardians won, while the Tigers lost, giving Cleveland the AL Central title. … (3) Cleveland Guardians (AL Central champions) vs. (6) Detroit Tigers (third wild card): Tigers won the series, 2–1.

mlb-guardians.text: Fun fact. The 1954 Indians won 111 games, then got swept in the World Series anyway. It's still the winningest season in franchise history. Yikes.
mlb-guardians.claim: 1954 Indians went 111–43 (winningest season in franchise history) and were swept in the World Series by the Giants.
mlb-guardians.proof: The winningest season in franchise history came in 1954, when the Indians finished the season with a record of 111–43 (.721). … The team could not bring home the title, however, ultimately being upset by the Giants in a sweep.

mlb-rockies.text: Fun fact. The Rockies finished 2025 at 43–119, tying for the third-most losses in the modern era. Somewhere, the 2003 Tigers had company.
mlb-rockies.claim: Colorado went 43–119 in 2025, tying for the third-most losses in the modern era (with the 2003 Tigers).
mlb-rockies.proof: the Rockies finished the season with 43 wins and 119 losses, tying for the third-most losses in the modern era with the 2003 Detroit Tigers

mlb-rockies.text: Fun fact. The 2025 Rockies posted a −424 run differential — the worst by any MLB team in the modern era, and the worst since the 1899 Cleveland Spiders.
mlb-rockies.claim: Colorado's 2025 run differential of −424 is the worst by any MLB team in the modern era and the worst since the 1899 Cleveland Spiders.
mlb-rockies.proof: The Rockies' −424 run differential is the worst by any MLB team in the modern era and the worst since the 1899 Cleveland Spiders.

mlb-rockies.text: Fun fact. Colorado lost 22 straight series, a major league record. Winning a series became a rare collectible in Denver.
mlb-rockies.claim: The Rockies lost 22 consecutive series in 2024–2025, a major league record.
mlb-rockies.proof: The Rockies lost a major league-record 22 straight series dating back to the previous September.

mlb-rockies.text: Fun fact. In 2025 the Rockies became the first team since their own 1999 squad to give up 1,000 runs in a season. Tradition runs deep.
mlb-rockies.claim: The 2025 Rockies allowed at least 1,000 runs, the first team to do so since the 1999 Rockies.
mlb-rockies.proof: the Rockies became the first team since their 1999 team to give up at least 1,000 runs to their opponents in a season.

mlb-rockies.text: Fun fact. The Rockies opened 2025 at 8–42 — the worst 50-game start in the era. Spring training apparently didn't take.
mlb-rockies.claim: Colorado opened the 2025 season 8–42 (.160), the worst 50-game start in the era.
mlb-rockies.proof: the Rockies opened to an 8–42 (.160) record through their first 50 games, marking the worst 50-game start in the era

mlb-tigers.text: Fun fact. The 2003 Tigers went 43–119 — the most losses in AL history — and came within one loss of the 1962 Mets' all-time mark. A masterpiece of futility.
mlb-tigers.claim: 2003 Tigers finished 43–119: most losses in American League history and one loss short of the 1962 Mets' record.
mlb-tigers.proof: the team finished with a record of 43–119, which surpassed the 1916 Philadelphia Athletics for the most losses in American League history (though not for the worst winning percentage) and came within one loss of tying the 1962 Mets of the National League for the most losses in modern major league history at the time.

mlb-tigers.text: Fun fact. The 2003 Tigers were swept 21 times and won exactly eight series all season. Eight. That's a sweep collection, not a schedule.
mlb-tigers.claim: 2003 Tigers were swept 21 times and had only eight series victories of their own.
mlb-tigers.proof: They were swept a total of 21 times while notching only eight series victories (by any margin) of their own.

mlb-tigers.text: Fun fact. By August 30, 2003, Detroit had already lost 100 games for the second straight season. Consistency is the Tigers' superpower.
mlb-tigers.claim: Tigers had lost 100 games for the second consecutive season by August 30, 2003.
mlb-tigers.proof: On August 30, after a 5–2 loss to the White Sox, the Tigers had lost 100 games for the second straight season

mlb-tigers.text: Fun fact. The 2025 Tigers went 7–17 in September and gave the division lead to Cleveland — a team that had been 15.5 games behind them in July.
mlb-tigers.claim: Tigers went 7–17 in September 2025 and gave up their division lead to Cleveland, a team 15.5 games behind them in early July.
mlb-tigers.proof: the Tigers faltered severely in the second half, going 28–37 since the All-Star Game and only 7–17 in September. They gave up their division lead to the Cleveland Guardians, a team that was 15.5 games behind them in early July

mlb-tigers.text: Fun fact. Detroit lost the 2025 ALDS in five games — the exact same ALDS exit as 2024. Déjà vu, Motor City.
mlb-tigers.claim: Tigers lost the 2025 ALDS in five games, repeating their 2024 ALDS result.
mlb-tigers.proof: Detroit repeated their 2024 ALDS performance, losing the series in five games.

mlb-astros.text: Fun fact. The Astros' first-ever World Series appearance, 2005, ended in a sweep — the White Sox dispatched them in four straight.
mlb-astros.claim: Verified on the Houston Astros Wikipedia page: their first World Series appearance (2005) ended in a sweep by the White Sox.
mlb-astros.proof: culminating in their first World Series appearance in 2005 where they were swept by the Chicago White Sox.

mlb-astros.text: Fun fact. The Astros lost more than 100 games three years in a row, ending with a franchise-worst 51–111 and a 15-game season-ending losing streak.
mlb-astros.claim: Verified on the Houston Astros Wikipedia page (2013 season section): three straight 100-loss seasons, 51–111 franchise-worst record, season-ending 15-game losing streak.
mlb-astros.proof: The Astros finished the season with a 51–111 record (a franchise-worst) with a season-ending 15-game losing streak, again surpassing their worst record from the previous season. The team finished 45 games behind the division winner Oakland Athletics, further adding to their futility. This marked three consecutive years that the Astros had lost more than 100 games in a single season.

mlb-astros.text: Fun fact. Houston's first World Series title, 2017, came with controversy and backlash from fans after the team was implicated in a sign stealing scandal.
mlb-astros.claim: Verified on the Houston Astros Wikipedia page: the 2017 World Series win (their first championship) drew controversy and backlash after the team was implicated in a sign stealing scandal.
mlb-astros.proof: During this era, the Astros won the 2017 World Series, their first championship, against the Los Angeles Dodgers; however, this win drew controversy and backlash from fans after the Astros were implicated in a sign stealing scandal.

mlb-astros.text: Fun fact. The 2019 World Series: the Astros went 0-4 at home against the Nationals, only winning the three games they played in Washington.
mlb-astros.claim: Verified on the Houston Astros Wikipedia page: lost the 2019 World Series in seven games, losing all four home games while winning three in Washington.
mlb-astros.proof: However, they lost the 2019 World Series to the Washington Nationals in seven games, taking three games in Washington but losing all four of their games at home.

mlb-astros.text: Fun fact. The Astros didn't post their first winning record until 1972 — and their first-ever playoff appearance didn't come until 1980.
mlb-astros.claim: Verified on the Houston Astros Wikipedia page: first winning record in 1972, first playoff appearance in 1980.
mlb-astros.proof: The Astros posted their first winning record in 1972 and made the playoffs for the first time in 1980

mlb-royals.text: Fun fact. Kansas City went 28 consecutive seasons (1986–2013) without a single playoff berth. Grandparents raised entire kids in that drought.
mlb-royals.claim: Royals missed the postseason for 28 consecutive seasons from 1986 to 2013, one of the longest wild-card-era droughts.
mlb-royals.proof: For 28 consecutive seasons (1986–2013), the Royals did not qualify to play in the MLB postseason, one of the longest postseason droughts during baseball's current wild-card era.

mlb-royals.text: Fun fact. From 1995 to 2012, the Royals had exactly one winning season: 2003. One. Frame it.
mlb-royals.claim: Royals had only one winning season (2003) from 1995 to 2012.
mlb-royals.proof: The team remained competitive throughout the early 1990s, but then had only one winning season (2003) from 1995 to 2012.

mlb-royals.text: Fun fact. The 2019 Royals' 59–103 record was one game BETTER than their 2018 record. Improvement, Royals style.
mlb-royals.claim: Royals finished the 2019 season at 59–103, one game better than their 2018 record.
mlb-royals.proof: The Royals finished the 2019 season one game better than 2018, at 59–103.

mlb-royals.text: Fun fact. The 2023 Royals went 56–106, tying the worst winning percentage in franchise history, and were mathematically out in August for the eighth straight year.
mlb-royals.claim: Royals eliminated from playoff contention August 29, 2023 (eighth consecutive season); 56–106 tied the lowest winning percentage (.346) in franchise history.
mlb-royals.proof: They were eliminated from playoff contention for the eighth consecutive season on August 29. Their 56–106 record tied the 2005 season for the lowest winning percentage (.346) in franchise history.

mlb-royals.text: Fun fact. The Royals lost the 2014 World Series finale by one run, 3–2, with the potential tying run standing on third base. Ninety feet of heartbreak.
mlb-royals.claim: Giants won the 2014 World Series final game 3–2; Royals' Gordon reached third base as the potential tying run.
mlb-royals.proof: The Giants won the final game, 3–2, thanks to timely hitting, including the game-winning RBI by Michael Morse to score Pablo Sandoval. … which allowed Gordon to reach third base as the potential tying run

mlb-angels.text: Fun fact. The Angels have not appeared in the postseason since 2014 — the longest active playoff drought of any MLB team.
mlb-angels.claim: Verified on the Los Angeles Angels Wikipedia page: no postseason appearance since 2014, the longest active playoff drought of any MLB team.
mlb-angels.proof: Despite this, they have not appeared in the postseason since 2014, the longest active playoff drought of any MLB team.

mlb-angels.text: Fun fact. The Angels became the last active MLB franchise to lose 100 games in a season, doing so in 2026. Better late than never?
mlb-angels.claim: Verified on the Los Angeles Angels Wikipedia page: they became the last active MLB franchise to lose 100 games in a season, doing so in 2026.
mlb-angels.proof: The Angels also became the last active MLB franchise to lose 100 games in a season, doing so in 2026.

mlb-angels.text: Fun fact. The Angels' founding owner never saw them win a World Series in his 38 years as owner — he'd been dead four years when they finally won in 2002.
mlb-angels.claim: Verified on the Los Angeles Angels Wikipedia page: Gene Autry never saw the Angels win a World Series in 38 years as owner; they won in 2002, four years after his death.
mlb-angels.proof: The saying refers to the Angels' founder and previous owner, Gene Autry, who never saw his Angels win a World Series in his 38 years as owner. Years went by as the team experienced many losses just strikes away from American League pennants. By the time the Angels won their first World Series in 2002, Autry had been dead for four years.

mlb-angels.text: Fun fact. In 1982 and 1986 the Angels came within one game of reaching the World Series — and in both years, they didn't get there.
mlb-angels.claim: Verified on the Los Angeles Angels Wikipedia page: came within one game of the World Series in both 1982 and 1986.
mlb-angels.proof: The Angels came within one game of reaching the World Series in 1982 and 1986.

mlb-angels.text: Fun fact. The Angels' entire World Series résumé is a single entry: 2002, their only championship appearance to date. One and done.
mlb-angels.claim: Verified on the Los Angeles Angels Wikipedia page: the 2002 World Series is their only championship appearance to date.
mlb-angels.proof: they would eventually achieve their first Wild Card spot in 2002 for their first postseason appearance since 1986 and used this momentum to win the 2002 World Series, their only championship appearance to date.

mlb-dodgers.text: Fun fact. The Dodgers' three-peat hopes ended in a four-game NLCS sweep by the Brewers, who went on to win the World Series.
mlb-dodgers.claim: Los Angeles was swept in the 2026 NLCS by the eventual champion Milwaukee Brewers, ending their bid to three-peat.
mlb-dodgers.proof: where they were swept by the eventual World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers in four games, ending their hopes of three-peating the World Series

mlb-dodgers.text: Fun fact. The Dodgers failed to become the first team to three-peat since the 2000 Yankees. Keep dreaming, LA.

mlb-rays.text: Fun fact. The Rays are one of just four MLB teams without a World Series title — and currently hold the most World Series appearances without winning one, at three.
mlb-rays.claim: Rays have zero World Series titles and the most World Series appearances (3) without a series win
mlb-rays.proof: The Rays are one of four MLB teams to not have a World Series title yet, the others being the San Diego Padres, Colorado Rockies, and Seattle Mariners, and are currently the team with the most World Series appearances without a series win with three appearances.

mlb-rays.text: Fun fact. In the Devil Rays' first decade they finished last in the AL East every year except 2004 — when they rose all the way to second to last.
mlb-rays.claim: Devil Rays finished last in AL East every year of their first decade except 2004 (second to last)
mlb-rays.proof: The team's first decade of play was marked by futility; they finished in last place in the AL East in all but the 2004 season, when they finished second to last.

mlb-rays.text: Fun fact. Tampa Bay's 2002 season led to a franchise-worst 55–106 record. Records are made to be broken — apparently not this one.
mlb-rays.claim: 2002 season ended with the franchise-worst 55-106 record
mlb-rays.proof: the 2002 season would lead to a franchise-worst 55–106 record, despite the emergence of key players like Aubrey Huff, Toby Hall, and Carl Crawford.

mlb-rays.text: Fun fact. The Rays reached the World Series again in 2026 and — once again — lost. At this point "again" is the franchise's favorite word.
mlb-rays.claim: Rays reached the 2026 World Series and lost, their third World Series loss
mlb-rays.proof: They reached the World Series again in 2026, but once again lost to the Milwaukee Brewers.

mlb-rays.text: Fun fact. Through 2026 the Rays' all-time record is 2,266–2,328 (.493) — the franchise has lost more games than it has ever won.
mlb-rays.claim: Rays all-time record through 2026 is 2,266-2,328 (.493), a losing record
mlb-rays.proof: Through 2026, the Rays' all-time record is 2,266–2,328 (.493).

mlb-rangers.text: Fun fact. In 2011 the Rangers were one strike away from winning the World Series — twice, in game six — and still lost the series to the Cardinals in seven.
mlb-rangers.claim: Verified on the Texas Rangers Wikipedia page: lost the 2011 World Series in seven games after twice being one strike away from winning it in game six.
mlb-rangers.proof: They repeated as American League champions in 2011, but lost the World Series to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games after twice being one strike away from winning the series in game six.

mlb-rangers.text: Fun fact. In the Rangers' first-ever World Series appearance, 2010, they fell to the San Francisco Giants in five games.
mlb-rangers.claim: Verified on the Texas Rangers Wikipedia page: in their first World Series appearance (2010) they fell to the Giants in five games.
mlb-rangers.proof: In their first appearance in a World Series, the Rangers fell to the San Francisco Giants in five games.

mlb-rangers.text: Fun fact. Back when this franchise was the Washington Senators, it never made the postseason — not once. Zero October trips in D.C.
mlb-rangers.claim: Verified on the Texas Rangers Wikipedia page: in the franchise's iteration as the Washington Senators, the team never made the postseason.
mlb-rangers.proof: The Rangers have made nine appearances in the MLB postseason (all as the Rangers—in their iteration as the Washington Senators, the team never made the postseason).

mlb-rangers.text: Fun fact. From 1961 through 2025, the Rangers franchise's all-time record is 4,899–5,383–6 (.476) — more losses than wins across its entire history.
mlb-rangers.claim: Verified on the Texas Rangers Wikipedia page: franchise all-time win-loss record from 1961 through 2025 is 4,899–5,383–6 (.476), a losing record.
mlb-rangers.proof: From 1961 through 2025, the franchise's overall win–loss record is 4,899–5,383–6 (.476).

mlb-rangers.text: Fun fact. The Rangers finished last in both 1972 and 1973 — the franchise's first winning season didn't arrive until 1974.
mlb-rangers.claim: Verified on the Texas Rangers Wikipedia page: finished last in both 1972 and 1973; first winning season in 1974.
mlb-rangers.proof: In 1974, the Rangers had their first winning season after finishing last in both 1972 and 1973.

mlb-bluejays.text: Fun fact. After their championship seasons, the Blue Jays failed to qualify for the playoffs for 21 consecutive seasons. Two titles, then two decades of nothing.
mlb-bluejays.claim: Blue Jays missed the playoffs for 21 consecutive seasons after their 1992-93 championships
mlb-bluejays.proof: Following their championship seasons, the Blue Jays failed to qualify for the playoffs for 21 consecutive seasons until clinching a playoff berth and division championship in 2015.

mlb-bluejays.text: Fun fact. In 2025 the Blue Jays made the World Series, lost to the Dodgers in seven games, and watched Game 7 slip into extra innings. So close, Canada.
mlb-bluejays.claim: Blue Jays lost the 2025 World Series to the Dodgers in seven games, with Game 7 going to extra innings
mlb-bluejays.proof: The Blue Jays reached the World Series, losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in seven games with Game 7 going into extra innings.

mlb-bluejays.text: Fun fact. In the late 1970s and early 1980s, the Blue Jays frequently finished last in their division. They set the tone early.
mlb-bluejays.claim: Blue Jays frequently finished last in their division in the late 1970s and early 1980s
mlb-bluejays.proof: In the late 1970s and early 1980s, the Blue Jays went through struggles typical of an expansion team, frequently finishing last in their division.

mlb-bluejays.text: Fun fact. The Blue Jays clinched back-to-back playoff berths in 2015-16, beat the Rangers in the Division Series both years, then lost the Championship Series both years.
mlb-bluejays.claim: In 2015 and 2016 the Blue Jays beat Texas in the AL Division Series but lost the AL Championship Series both years
mlb-bluejays.proof: The team clinched a second consecutive playoff berth in 2016, after securing an AL wild card position. In both years, the Blue Jays beat the Texas Rangers in the AL Division Series, but lost the AL Championship Series.

mlb-bluejays.text: Fun fact. From 1977 to 2026, the Blue Jays' overall win-loss record is 3,934–3,939–3 (.500). Nearly 50 years of baseball, still losing more than winning.
mlb-bluejays.claim: Blue Jays all-time record from 1977 to 2026 is 3,934-3,939-3 (.500), a losing record
mlb-bluejays.proof: From 1977 to 2026, the Blue Jays' overall win-loss record is 3,934–3,939–3 (.500).

mlb-nationals.text: Fun fact. After trading Juan Soto and others, the Nationals finished the 2022 season with the worst record in baseball at 55–107.
mlb-nationals.claim: After trading Juan Soto and others, the Nationals finished the 2022 season with the worst record in baseball, 55–107.
mlb-nationals.proof: After trading Soto and others, the Nationals finished the 2022 season with the worst record in baseball at 55–107.

mlb-nationals.text: Fun fact. The Nationals traded 23-year-old superstar Juan Soto away, losing their franchise icon and one of the last integral players from the 2019 championship team.
mlb-nationals.claim: On August 2, 2022, the Nationals traded 23-year-old superstar Juan Soto to the Padres, losing their franchise icon and one of the last integral players from the 2019 championship team.
mlb-nationals.proof: On August 2, 2022, the Nationals sent 23-year-old superstar Juan Soto to the San Diego Padres in a blockbuster trade after he turned down a 15-year, $440 million contract extension offer, which would have constituted the richest contract in baseball history. In doing so, the Nationals lost its franchise icon and one of the last integral players from the 2019 championship team.

mlb-nationals.text: Fun fact. The Nationals finished in last place in four out of five years from 2006 to 2010.
mlb-nationals.claim: The Nationals finished in last place in four out of five years from 2006 to 2010.
mlb-nationals.proof: The Nationals finished in last place in four out of five years from 2006 to 2010, but began building the foundations of a contender with their first-overall draft picks of pitcher Stephen Strasburg (in 2009) and catcher Bryce Harper, whom the team converted to the outfield, (in 2010), as well as their sixth-overall draft pick of infielder Anthony Rendon (in 2011).

mlb-nationals.text: Fun fact. The Nationals won the NL East in 2014, 2016, and 2017, but failed to advance past the NLDS each time.
mlb-nationals.claim: The Nationals won the National League East in 2014, 2016, and 2017 but failed to advance past the NLDS each time.
mlb-nationals.proof: The team secured their first playoff berth and first division title in 2012 and won the National League East again in 2014, 2016, and 2017, but failed to advance past the NLDS each time.

mlb-nationals.text: Fun fact. In 2025, the Nationals fired manager Dave Martinez and general manager Mike Rizzo, then finished the season with a disappointing 66–96 record.
mlb-nationals.claim: On July 6, 2025, the Nationals fired manager Dave Martinez and general manager Mike Rizzo, then finished the 2025 season with a disappointing 66–96 record.
mlb-nationals.proof: On July 6, 2025, following a disappointing first half of the 2025 season below internal projections for the rebuild, the Nationals fired manager Dave Martinez and general manager Mike Rizzo ... The Nationals finished the 2025 season with a disappointing 66–96 record.
